data.statement: Always write and push project memory directly to the Omnigraph graph/branch matching the repository folder name (OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID=<repo-folder-name>), and never to the shared 'memory' graph.

data.rationale: Per the one-graph-per-repo isolation model (as-dec-per-project-split-executed), AutoOS is declared in cluster.yaml graphs: and added to the project-graphs-access policy bundle, so its structured memory is isolated from the shared memory graph and from every other project. Declaring it does not make it live: scripts/apply-cluster.sh must run against the target server, and graphs_list on that server is the check (as-rule-declared-is-not-live).
data.title: AutoOS gets its own Omnigraph graph

data.rationale: Generalised from four failures of one shape in a single downstream session: one layer was changed and a coupled one left behind. A merge renumbered files while the job database still named the old paths -- and one of those old paths still EXISTED and held the pre-merge file, so staging re-fetched it over the new one. Ids were corrected in one store while two upstream sources kept the old ones, so the next sync restored them. Work was re-queued while its previous results stayed in place, and the integrity guard then refused every item. A hand-edited input left its derived fields frozen, and gigabytes were written under a placeholder name. Principle 8 adds the sharper lesson: fix the CONDITION, not the instances -- clearing only the records that had already failed left the not-yet-run ones to fail identically on the next pass. Principle 9 covers verification that proves nothing: every acceptance check called a resolver with the argument that makes it SKIP its authoritative source and fall back to a filename, so 60 of 60 'verified' while the path production takes was never exercised. Its corollary: never pipe a long-running command through grep/tail, because buffering loses the traceback and a broken run reads as a silent one.
data.title: Coding principles 8 (coupled state) and 9 (authoritative path)

data.rationale: ADR 0004 (2026-07-30). Audit prompted by Cursor's 'Agent Swarms and Model Economics' (identical completion varied ~8x in cost purely by planner/worker model split; workers are 69-90% of tokens but a minority of cost; scaling comes from context efficiency, not parallelism) and Rahul Garg's 'The Orchestrator's Tax' (the cost of subagents is context pollution, not tokens - tokens are spent once, context shapes every decision that follows; prefer 2-4 agents per wave, never poll full transcripts, no repo-wide git during concurrent work). The finding was NOT that the policy was wrong: contract-first handoff with hash drift detection, a different-family reviewer, frontier-planner plus mid-tier-worker routing, and worktree-per-engineer isolation were already aligned with both articles. Two things were wrong. (1) Nothing enforced the policy on the surface actually driven - day-to-day orchestration runs through Claude Code native Agent/Workflow and the repo shipped ZERO .claude/agents, ZERO .claude/workflows and ZERO hooks; skills/*/agents/*.yaml are OpenAI Codex manifests, not Claude subagent definitions; the Python scaffold that did encode the policy had never run outside stub mode. (2) Several facts had more than one home and had already drifted: risk thresholds disagreed three ways between SKILL.md, the YAML and RiskEngine.score() (which divides by weight_sum, making it a mean not the documented sum); the verdict matrix existed in three places with the YAML copy read by no code at all; reviewer model tiers were pinned to ids two generations stale. Decision: Markdown declares and generated artifacts enforce; agent_orchestration.config.yaml is the single runtime source and the .claude adapter is GENERATED from it with a --check drift gate, because workflow scripts have no filesystem access and cannot read YAML at runtime; a response schema is the context firewall because a schema'd agent physically cannot return a transcript; wave caps are two-tier; and different_family_from_engineer splits by surface. Consequences: AGENT_ORCHESTRATION_FRAMEWORK.md deleted (it restated SKILL.md and the YAML almost in full), CUSTOM_ORCHESTRATION_VS_OPENHANDS.md became ADR 0005, SKILL.md rewritten to hold no numbers. Rejected: telemetry-first (needs a cluster schema change for a metered-run node type, deferred to its own ADR) and adopting Cursor's reconciler/megafile-decomposer/Field-Guide/custom-VCS wholesale (they solve failures at ~1000 commits/sec across dozens of planners; at 2-5 agents worktrees plus TTL locks already prevent those collisions). Design approved, implementation PENDING - see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-orchestration-context-and-economics-design.md.
data.title: Orchestration policy must be executable, and the config owns every number

data.rationale: graphifyy[mcp] leaves the mcp SDK unpinned. mcp 2.0.0 split its type exports into mcp-types and dropped AnyUrl from mcp.types, which graphify 0.9.20 imports at server-build time, so an unconstrained install crashes on startup with ImportError: cannot import name 'AnyUrl'. In Claude Code that surfaces only as graphify 'Failed to connect -- Connection closed', with no hint of the real cause. infra/mcp-servers/servers/graphify-mcp/Dockerfile caps it below 2.0 and adds the openai extra; the image must be rebuilt after the pin: docker build -t graphify-mcp:latest infra/mcp-servers/servers/graphify-mcp.
data.title: Pin mcp<2 for graphify's MCP server

data.rationale: graphify.serve is stdio and reads a static graphify-out/graph.json, inheriting its launch directory, so a SINGLE user-scope `graphify` entry with the relative path serves whichever repo you start Claude Code in. Workstation uses `uv`; a server (coding.example.internal) uses the tracked infra/mcp-servers/bin/graphify-mcp wrapper injecting -v "$PWD:/repo" because MCP args are not shell-expanded. This retires the 2026-07-19 per-repo `graphify-docker` project entries, whose hardcoded mount made one repo's graph answer for every repo. Omnigraph stays per-repo (project scope, OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID) because each repo is a distinct graph on a shared server; graphify does not, being a local cwd-selected file. agent-skills documents this as the way, being the template repo. Verified: PowerShell check-graphify-scope exits 0 across the code root and a raw MCP handshake serves this repo's own graph.
data.title: Graphify is one cwd-relative user-scope MCP entry, not per-repo

data.rationale: Completing per-project isolation: after copying all 4 projects into their own graphs and verifying the reconcile (160 project nodes + 2 globals = 162 = memory; 163/163 edges), the 160 project nodes were deleted from `memory` (edges cascade on node delete). `memory` is now 2 nodes / 0 edges and matches cluster/seed/memory.jsonl. Pruning is gated by split-project-graph.py --prune-source, which refuses unless every node is mirrored, with the same type, in its project graph.
data.title: The `memory` graph holds ONLY global-scope Preferences

data.rationale: d0607bf declared 5 graphs + 5 relational edge types but nothing had applied them: the live server ran one `memory` graph on the old schema, so Tracks/Affects/Addresses/Implements/DependsOn were rejected and every seed line using them failed silently. Root cause: apply-cluster.sh sourced a ./.env that never existed (convention is .env.shared + .env.server) so it died at line 15 under set -e and had never run. Fixed the script (env files, docker network mcp-server_mcp-net, MSYS path conversion), converged the cluster, repaired 7 orphaned hub edges, and split all 4 projects into their own graphs with the new split-project-graph.py. Verified: 160 project nodes + 2 global Preferences = 162 = memory; 163/163 edges.
data.title: Per-project graph isolation deployed and back-filled (2026-07-16)

data.rationale: Measured 2026-08-21 on the site-repo graph: four update mutations each returned affectedNodes: 1 AND were each confirmed by an immediate read showing the new value; about an hour later all four had reverted, while inserts from the same window survived. An unattributable commit sits in between (actorId is 'default' on every commit and commits_get returns metadata only), so the cause is recorded as UNPROVEN rather than guessed at. What holds regardless: check commits_list head before/after, re-read important writes at the END of a session, and prefer inserting a new node over updating one when the content must not be lost. The same session also promoted a confident wrong rule from correlated failures -- 'never mix update and insert, the updates are silently dropped' -- which a throwaway-branch test disproved in minutes and which contradicted an already-verified rule. Recorded in skills/structured-memory/references/operations.md rule 6.
data.title: Read-back is not proof of durability; falsify before documenting

data.rationale: ADR 0003 (2026-07-16). The off-by-default mem0-fallback profile was never exercised, yet kept leaking back into docs and per-repo instructions as a live option (sibling-analysis-repo wired mem0 and no omnigraph at all while claiming 'Memory is Omnigraph now'). A fallback with a different data model is not a fallback: Mem0 stores blobs by user_id, Omnigraph stores typed nodes/edges, nothing migrates, so falling back meant losing the graph. It cost 4 containers (Postgres/pgvector, API, bridge, dashboard), a POSTGRES_PASSWORD, a DeepSeek key, and a second embedding model (bge-m3 1024-dim next to the graph's 768-dim nomic-embed-text — a standing dimension-mismatch trap). Its tooling had already rotted: the setup/start/stop/test/migrate scripts still health-checked mem0 on :8888 and their bare `docker compose` calls failed after the server/client compose split. Removed: servers/_fallback/, the compose profile + 4 services, the mem0/Postgres/DeepSeek env vars, the Mem0-era scripts, and the legacy docs/ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/TOKEN_SAVINGS.md. The stack now needs no Postgres and no LLM API key; Ollama stays optional. Insurance is backups (cluster/seed/*.jsonl, .graph-backup/ exports, MinIO), not a parallel product.
data.title: Remove the Mem0 fallback entirely — Omnigraph has no fallback

data.rationale: init-serena-projects.{sh,ps1} used to pin the same 16 languages into every repo's project.yml. That is actively harmful on Serena 1.5.3: LanguageServerManager fails all-or-nothing, so ONE language server that cannot start disables every symbolic tool for the whole project (find_symbol, get_symbols_overview, the lot), not just that language's. The scripts now walk the repo pruning vendored/build/cache dirs at any depth, map file extensions to Serena languages, order them most-prevalent-first (the first becomes Serena's default/fallback), and drop any compiled language whose toolchain is not on PATH. csharp is special-cased: dotnet merely existing is not enough -- Serena's C# LSP needs .NET runtime 10.x, checked via dotnet --list-runtimes matching Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.*. --force must remove project.yml first, because serena project create hard-refuses when one exists and offers no overwrite flag. Batch mode (--code-root) is opt-in and never the default, because it touches every git repo under a shared code root.
data.title: Serena project.yml is generated per repo by language autodetection, not a fixed language list

data.rationale: The viewer Sync log's 'source' column read `default` for every device. Determined against a live omnigraph v0.8.1 server: a commit record carries only graph_commit_id/created_at/actor_id/manifest_*/parent ids and NO client address, and the server logs no request IPs, so a past push's origin is simply not recorded. actor_id is resolved from the BEARER TOKEN via an actor->token map (OMNIGRAPH_SERVER_BEARER_TOKENS_JSON / _FILE / _AWS_SECRET); proved on a throwaway cluster that two tokens yield two actor_ids, an actor missing from the policy group gets 403 and an unknown token 401. The CLI's --as flag is a red herring: its own help says 'no effect on remote writes (the server resolves the actor from the bearer token)'. Making actor_id vary would therefore need a bearer token per device - a secret to distribute and rotate on every machine - which was rejected. The only identity a device supplies for free is its TCP source address, so the sync POSTs /api/sync-ping?graph=<g> after each graph and the viewer records what it observes: source IP -> device via OMNIGRAPH_DEVICE_MAP, else reverse DNS, else the bare IP.
data.title: Attribute syncs by source IP, because actor_id can never name the device

data.rationale: OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID pins a bridge to exactly one graph and no tool (query/mutate/load) accepts a graph argument, so under per-project isolation an agent physically cannot reach the shared `memory` graph its skill tells it to recall globals from. Resolution: declare two servers per repo — `omnigraph` (OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID=<repo>, read+write) and `omnigraph-globals` (OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID=memory, read-only). Recorded in structured-memory/SKILL.md and both starters.
data.title: Reading global Preferences requires a second omnigraph MCP bridge

data.name: Omnigraph cluster (declared config + live store)

data.statement: No Decision in the agent-skills graph is vector-searchable today, and writing one through mutate insert does NOT fix that. Verified 2026-08-24 on a throwaway branch: a freshly inserted Decision reads back with embedding: null; order { nearest($d.embedding, $q) } limit 5 returns 0 rows across all 11 Decisions on main; and herdr-multiplexer, which had a vector on 2026-07-16, is now null. This EXTENDS as-rule-embed-after-merge, which covered only load --mode merge -- insert is no better, so there is no write path that embeds. Consequence: recall this graph by traversal and full-text only, never claim semantic search covers its decisions, and do not spend time re-embedding in place -- on v0.8.1 the only working path is a rebuild through scripts/dedup-graph.py into an empty store.

The .claude/ adapter (agents, workflows, hooks) is GENERATED from agent_orchestration.config.yaml by skills/swarm-orchestration/tools/gen_claude_adapter.py and must never be hand-edited - generated files carry a DO NOT EDIT header and the generator's --check mode gates drift in pre-commit. Generation is not a style choice: Claude Code workflow scripts have no filesystem access and no require/import, so they cannot read the YAML at runtime, and a hand-written adapter would put model tiers and review lenses in two places that then drift. The three reviewer agent files are derived from swarm_review.perspectives, so adding a lens is a one-line config change.

Declared cluster config is NOT live until scripts/apply-cluster.sh runs against the target server. Before trusting cluster.yaml or memory.pg, verify against the live server: graphs_list must list the declared graphs and schema_get must show the declared edge types. A seed or mutation using an undeclared edge type fails silently.

A merge-loaded Decision is NOT semantically searchable, and on v0.8.1 you cannot fix it in place. `load --mode merge` does not compute the @embed("rationale") vector, and merging a Decision that HAD one ERASES it (the upsert replaces the row) — an unembedded Decision is dropped from nearest() entirely, not ranked low. Verified 2026-07-16: both re-embed paths fail with the same Lance bug on a populated graph (`overwrite` -> stage_create_btree_index; `merge` carrying hand-supplied vectors -> LanceError(Arrow) same-length), and `omnigraph embed --reembed_all` cannot target a local endpoint. So scripts/populate-embeddings.py only works against a fresh/empty graph. Treat this as a known limitation: the node stays findable by traversal and full-text; the only re-embed path is a rebuild via scripts/dedup-graph.py (which reloads into an empty store). Never claim semantic search covers a Decision you merged without confirming with a nearest() query.

Do not promote a mechanism from correlated failures into written guidance without falsifying it first, and do not treat affectedNodes or an immediate read-back as proof that a write is durable. A new rule that contradicts an already-verified one is a signal to TEST, not to write. branches_create -> probe -> branches_delete makes that test free and safe, and is the required step before documenting any Omnigraph mechanism. Verify writes with commits_list head before/after, re-read important writes at session END, and prefer inserting a new node over updating one when the content must not be lost.

Never install or rebuild graphifyy[mcp] without capping mcp<2. The dependency is unpinned upstream and mcp 2.x dropped AnyUrl from mcp.types, which graphify imports at server-build time; the only symptom Claude Code shows is graphify 'Failed to connect -- Connection closed'. Applies to the Docker image (infra/mcp-servers/servers/graphify-mcp/Dockerfile, rebuild after changing) and to any uv/uvx install of the same extra.

Graphify is wired as exactly ONE cwd-relative `graphify` entry in USER scope (workstation `uv`; server `graphify-mcp` wrapper). Never give graphify a per-repo project-scope .mcp.json entry and never a hardcoded bind mount (that serves one repo's graph to all). Omnigraph, by contrast, IS per-repo. Verify with infra/mcp-servers/scripts/*/check-graphify-scope.*

Claude Code's Agent tool spawns only Claude, so native orchestration CANNOT deliver the different_family_from_engineer diversity that model_routing.reviewer asks for - fable is a different model but the same family, sharing training-derived blind spots. Native review gets LENS diversity only (security / performance / XP at differing tiers). Genuine FAMILY diversity is a herdr-orchestration capability (codex, cursor, droid, opencode in persistent panes) and is one of the four things native tooling cannot do. Do not claim family diversity on the native surface: three reviewers sharing a family also share their blind spots, so the claim produces false confidence in coverage.

Omnigraph is the only memory layer — there is no fallback. If it is down, work the session without recall (read the repo, CHANGELOG, ADRs) and persist when it returns; never stand up a side-channel store. Memory is an accelerator, not a correctness dependency. Recovery order: cluster/seed/*.jsonl (the boot seeder re-merges them), then a .graph-backup/ NDJSON export, then MinIO's bind-mounted store.

skills/swarm-orchestration/SKILL.md is normative policy and must contain NO numbers. Every threshold, weight, model tier, matrix, wave cap, checkpoint field and cache block lives in custom_orchestration/agent_orchestration.config.yaml, which SKILL.md section 0 maps. A number in the skill is a bug - it is how the risk thresholds came to disagree three ways (skill said raw sum with bands 0.60/0.85, YAML said 0.30/0.60/0.85, and RiskEngine.score divided by weight_sum making it a mean). Same rule for AGENT_ORCHESTRATION_RATIONALE.md: it answers WHY and any number in it is illustrative only.

Keep cluster/seed/*.jsonl in sync with live before relying on them: the seed loader merges by @key(slug) on every boot, so a stale seed silently overwrites newer live values. Refresh with scripts/split-project-graph.py <project> --write-seed.

Pin a language in .serena/project.yml only when its language server can actually start. Serena 1.5.3's LanguageServerManager fails all-or-nothing, so ONE unstartable server disables every symbolic tool for the WHOLE project, not just that language's. Compiled languages need their toolchain on PATH (go, rustc, clangd, java); csharp needs more than dotnet existing -- Serena's C# LSP requires .NET runtime 10.x specifically, so guard on dotnet --list-runtimes showing Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.* and skip csharp on a 6.x/8.x-only install. Restart the MCP server after changing project.yml: config is read only at startup.

Serena's project.yml language key is VERSION-COUPLED and a mismatch fails silently for the whole workstation. Versions <=1.6.1 read data['languages'] (1.5.3's resources/project.template.yml writes languages:); 1.7.0 renamed the key to language_servers: and its back-compat shim only maps the OLDER singular `language` forward -- nothing maps language_servers backward. Hand a 1.7.0-written file to a 1.5.3 server and it logs 'Failed to load project configuration ... KeyError: languages. This project will be skipped', reports 'Available projects:' EMPTY, and activate_project returns a bare KeyError - 'languages' -- every symbolic tool dead, in every repo, with nothing visibly wrong in project.yml. Verified 2026-08-24: 32 of 34 repos under the code root (agent-skills and sibling-analysis-repo included) carry language_servers: written on 2026-08-19, while the process actually serving MCP was 1.5.3 out of AppData/Roaming/uv/tools/serena-agent. The user-scope ~/.claude.json entry pins uvx --from serena-agent==1.7.0, but an MCP process started before that pin keeps serving the old build until Claude Code restarts -- so 'the pin is set' is not evidence of what is running. Pin FORWARD in user scope (a project .mcp.json cannot win against a same-named user-scope server), never edit the YAML backward. Diagnose from the server's OWN startup log (~/.serena/logs/<date>/mcp_*.txt), never by reading project.yml, and check without restarting via PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 uvx --from serena-agent==<v> serena project health-check . redirected to a file. General form: a KeyError on a key the config genuinely lacks means TWO VERSIONS of the tool, not a corrupt config -- confirm the rename direction by grepping the installed runtime's source.

DO NOT trust the Python scaffold's swarm review verdict until D1-D3 in the 2026-07-30 design spec are fixed - it returns APPROVE unconditionally and SILENTLY. Chain: ReviewerPanel.execute_swarm passes preferred_provider=details.get('model_tier'), i.e. the string 'sonnet-3.5' into a parameter whose domain is provider ids; ProviderRegistry.get raises KeyError on it; and adapter_for() sits at the top of the for-loop OUTSIDE the try that begins at execution_mode, so the KeyError escapes and aborts the whole 3-deep fallback chain at iteration 0 (this breaks fallback for ANY unknown provider name, not just this one); even on success execute_swarm returns perspective envelopes with no severity key while calculate_verdict reads finding.get('severity','low'), counting everything low. narration.mode=silent then returns None for APPROVE, so nothing is emitted. A safety gate that cannot fail closed.

Sync attribution must never guess. Attribute a commit only to a ping that FOLLOWS it within PING_WINDOW_SEC (default 900); leave older commits blank rather than inferring, because a wrong device name is worse than none. The ping is best-effort and must never fail a sync. Store only server-observed values (source IP, arrival time) plus a graph id validated against the cluster, and write under an flock'd atomic replace - gunicorn runs 2 workers and a plain read-modify-write loses raced records. Never read actor_id as the device: it is the shared token's actor and reads `default` for every client.

DO NOT enable omnigraph-sync.timer or dedup-graph.timer until both are multi-graph aware. omnigraph-sync.sh/sync-windows.ps1 sync exactly one graph (GRAPH defaults to `memory`) and step 5 pulls central into local with `load --mode overwrite` -- pointing a pruned local at a stale central RESTORES the pruned data and undoes the migration. dedup-graph.py hardcodes `--graph memory` in 3 places. Consequence today: the 4 project graphs are never synced to central and exist only on the client that created them.

Wave caps are two-tier because two different things bind them, and a single blanket number is wrong in both directions. A CONTEXT-SHARING wave (review lenses, exploration, orientation - output enters the orchestrator's reasoning) is bound by ATTENTION: cap 4, consolidate at 5+, never pull a full transcript to answer a lightweight status question, and treat overlapping file ownership as a consolidation signal rather than a locking problem. An ISOLATED CANDIDATE wave (Best-of-N: worktree + schema'd return + deterministic arbitration) never enters the orchestrator's working memory, so the attention argument does not apply and what binds it is worker-tier COST: cap 5, gated on objective arbitration being available. Applying Garg's literal 2-4 everywhere would delete Best-of-5 for the wrong reason.
